customManagers.description: Versions with a `# renovate: datasource=... depName=... [extractVersion=...]` comment on the line above
Kustomize resources that point at GitHub release assets, e.g. the system-upgrade-controller manifests

packageRules.description: Images and OCI charts in the manifests are pinned as tag@sha256:digest, so a re-pushed tag can't change what runs. The tag and digest are updated together.
Only Docker Hub gives docker release timestamps, so images and OCI charts from any other registry (GHCR, Quay) can't be aged. Without this, timestamp-required would hold them forever.
system-upgrade-controller: the release manifests and the image pinned in its kustomization.yaml move together.
Calendar versions YYYY.MM.N: a new year is a major, a new month a minor, N a patch. Also skips the -arm64 and build tags.
The Flux Operator chart is pinned in flux-operator.yaml and bootstrap.sh. Bump both in one commit.
k3s versions look like v1.36.5+k3s1: a new Kubernetes minor is a minor, patches and k3sN rebuilds are patches.
Every non-major update except fugleramme lands in one weekly PR, merged by hand.
The Gateway API CRDs have to match what Traefik's kubernetesGateway provider supports, so a minor gets its own PR.
Kubernetes upgrades one minor at a time and needs the charts to support it, so a k3s minor gets its own PR.
fugleramme is first-party: every release, majors and re-pushed tags too, goes straight to main once CI is green, at any time. It also publishes major.minor tags like 0.29; only follow full versions.
The upgrade Plan's image has no tag: the controller appends the Plan's version, so it can't carry a digest.
